title: Language and Glasshouse
premise: After his mother's funeral, Sebastian Ashgrove returns to the glasshouse her family built and finds a letter from Mirela Voss, the last fluent speaker of a dying language his mother secretly studied for decades. As Sebastian becomes her final student, he uncovers recordings, photographs, and letters revealing his mother's betrayal of Mirela decades ago — and discovers he himself was raised on words whose meanings were hidden from him. When the city announces the old neighborhood's demolition and the last bus route is rerouted, Sebastian must choose between cataloging the past and living it. He ends by teaching Mirela's language to neighborhood children in the glasshouse, forgiving both his mother and himself.
about_author: Ada Ishikawa is a former lexicographer who spent six years documenting endangered languages before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted greenhouse in the north of England, where she keeps her grandmother's untranslated letters on the windowsill.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Silence
chapters.summary: Sebastian, numb after the funeral, catalogs his mother's belongings like an estate agent rather than a son. In the glasshouse he finds a locked drawer and a photograph of two young women he doesn't recognize. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: grief expressed as bureaucratic distance; the first crack in it.

chapters.title: A Letter Addressed to No One
chapters.summary: Among the papers is an unopened letter from 'M.V.' dated thirty years ago. Sebastian tracks down the return address to a shuttered community center in the old neighborhood. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: curiosity overriding avoidance — the tenant begins inspecting the property.

chapters.title: Mirela Voss Speaks
chapters.summary: Sebastian finds Mirela, ninety-one, tending plants in a municipal conservatory. She mistakes him briefly for his mother, then says: 'You have her ears. Come learn what she refused to hear.' POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: vertigo — being claimed by a stranger's history.

chapters.title: First Words
chapters.summary: First lesson: Mirela teaches greetings and names, insisting language lives only in mouths, not notebooks. Sebastian records everything compulsively. A memory surfaces of his mother humming an unfamiliar lullaby. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: tentative wonder shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Glasshouse Grew
chapters.summary: Sebastian researches the family glasshouse and learns his grandfather employed immigrant workers from Mirela's community — including, perhaps, her sister. The photographs begin to make partial sense. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: inherited guilt arriving without instructions.

chapters.title: The Word for Return
chapters.summary: Mirela teaches the word for 'return,' which also means 'to owe.' She watches Sebastian too closely when he repeats it. Flashback chapter: 1979, young Mirela and Sebastian's mother, Elena, as friends. POV: alternating Sebastian / Mirela. Emotional beat: warmth with a hairline fracture running through it.

chapters.title: Tapes Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Sebastian discovers reel-to-reel tapes in the glasshouse foundation: Elena recording Mirela's vocabulary secretly, years of it. One tape cuts off mid-argument. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: betrayal discovered secondhand; the archive becomes evidence.

chapters.title: The Rerouting Notice
chapters.summary: City notices appear: the old neighborhood will be demolished; the last bus route rerouted in four months. Mirela refuses to leave. Sebastian realizes the deadline applies to more than buses. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: external clock starts ticking; stakes become concrete.

chapters.title: Elena's Margins
chapters.summary: In Elena's annotated grammar books, Sebastian finds marginal notes in Mirela's language — his mother could speak it fluently and never told him. His childhood lullabies reassemble into sentences. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: the stranger in the photographs acquires a face; anger blooms.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Conservatory
chapters.summary: Sebastian accuses Mirela of using him to punish Elena. Mirela counters: Elena didn't steal the language — she stole the credit, publishing a dictionary under her own name that made rescue funding impossible for the community school. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: both truths collide; no clean villain.

chapters.title: The Dictionary
chapters.summary: Sebastian reads Elena's published dictionary cover to cover and finds the acknowledgments blank where names should be. He understands the silence he inherited was authored. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: mourning shifts from mother to the mother he thought existed.

chapters.title: Mirela's Version
chapters.summary: Mirela narrates the full rupture: the friendship, the recordings, the publication, the twenty-year silence. She admits she wrote the unanswered letter out of loneliness, not blame. POV: Mirela. Emotional beat: grief given its own voice; the reader's sympathy rebalances.

chapters.title: Tenants
chapters.summary: Sebastian confronts his own life — the flat he never furnished, the job he quit attending — and recognizes he has been a tenant everywhere, including inside his own name. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: turning inward; the inheritance question becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Last Regular Service
chapters.summary: Riding the bus route slated for cancellation, Sebastian meets former neighbors who share fragments of the language and their memories of Elena among them. The community was always larger than two women's quarrel. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: belonging glimpsed from a bus window.

chapters.title: A Proposal in Winter Light
chapters.summary: Sebastian proposes republishing the dictionary under both names, with Mirela's corrections, and reopening the glasshouse as a free language school. Mirela neither accepts nor refuses. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: hope offered cautiously, like a hand across a table.

chapters.title: The Publisher's Objection
chapters.summary: The original publisher resists reattribution; legal and archival obstacles mount. Sebastian risks his small inheritance fighting the estate's copyright claims. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: rising tension — doing right costs something real.

chapters.title: Mirela Falters
chapters.summary: Mirela is hospitalized after a fall; her speech blurs between languages. At her bedside, Sebastian speaks to her in her tongue for the first time unprompted. She corrects his grammar gently. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: fear of losing the teacher before becoming the student fully.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Tape
chapters.summary: Restored, Mirela gives Sebastian the missing final tape: Elena's apology, recorded but never sent, asking forgiveness in the language itself. Sebastian finally hears his mother speak. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: climax of understanding — the apology was always there, waiting to be played.

chapters.title: Forgiving the Stranger
chapters.summary: At the glasshouse, Sebastian plays Elena's apology aloud and adds his own. He forgives the woman in the photographs — not excusing her, but releasing the debt. Mirela answers in the old formula for reconciliation. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: catharsis; the quarrel ends one generation late.

chapters.title: Last Bus, Old Route
chapters.summary: On the route's final day, Sebastian and Mirela ride it end to end with neighbors singing in the dying language. The demolition notice on the community center is photographed, archived, mourned. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: elegy and celebration braided together.

chapters.title: The Glasshouse Reopens
chapters.summary: Spring: the corrected dictionary is printed under both names. Children gather in the glasshouse for the first lesson; Mirela leads, Sebastian translates. The building is warm again. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: resolution — ownership reclaimed through stewardship, not possession.

chapters.title: The Word for Begin
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Mirela teaches the word for 'begin,' which contains the root for 'remember.' Sebastian writes his mother's true name into the record and hums the lullaby, finally knowing what it says. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: quiet continuation — memory kept alive by being spoken forward.
